**The real difference:** merge keeps your history exactly as it happened, with all the branching. Rebase rewrites your history to look like you built your changes on top of the latest main, in a straight line.

Merge is safe on anything shared — it never rewrites commits other people already have. Rebase changes commit hashes, so it's only safe on branches nobody else has pulled.

Reach for **merge** when you're bringing a finished feature branch back into main, especially if others have based work on it.

Reach for **rebase** when you're updating your own in-progress branch with the latest main, or cleaning up your commits before opening a PR — it keeps the log readable, one line, no merge bubbles.

Simple rule: rebase your own unpushed or solo work, merge anything shared.
